title: Code that cites kb lines by number (bench_core.py) no longer blocks a content item from inserting a fact
goal: A content item may add or remove a line in an article or ledger that _tools code cites by path:line (bench_core.py cites _conflicts.md and ci-and-headless.md) without check.py failing on a file outside its touches: the code cites by anchor or the citation is rewritten by the tool that moves the line, or planning puts the citing file in the item's touches (SP-df2cu4uj: BG-3bjktw5x broke bench_core.py:36 by adding a line, BG-rtqshnro skipped a planned fact for that reason).
notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 5 of 19, "Benchmark measurement: percentiles, a comparable router arm, a spend cap that holds and a corrected report"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. Premise: check.code_citation_errors fails on a file outside a content item's touches when the item inserts a fact line above a line _tools/bench_core.py cites. Run at planning on a scratch copy (bench_core.py, _conflicts.md, ci-and-headless.md): one tagged line inserted at line 11 of ci-and-headless.md raised the citation errors from 3 (files not copied) to 11. The test goes in test_check_programs.py, which already tests code_citation_errors; the choice among anchor, rewrite and touches is the worker's, the check needs one behaviour test of it.
